headline: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
briefing: Top stories right now: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya; CUPE Ontario education workers vote in favour of strike action ahead of bargaining; and Olivia Chow declined her seat on the Toronto police board.

keyDates.label: Trump meets Xi and Putin
keyDates.why: Trump holds a one-on-one with Xi and then a first-ever three-way meeting with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, with nuclear weapons the stated focus.

keyDates.label: Senate Democrats vote; Stelco recall
keyDates.why: Democratic senators choose between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for majority leader by secret ballot, and 175 laid-off Stelco workers are due back in Hamilton.

keyDates.label: Bank of Canada and Fed rate decisions
keyDates.why: Both central banks decide the same day; the Bank of Canada has said more hikes are possible.

keyDates.label: U.S. government funding deadline
keyDates.why: Federal funding runs out unless the outgoing Congress passes a spending bill or a temporary extension, which is also the likeliest vehicle for any new air traffic control money.

stories.headline: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
stories.summary: A historic judgment from the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. The ruling comes years after Myanmar's Muslim minority was forced to flee.

stories.headline: Ontario man on list of Canada's 25 most wanted fugitives arrested in Winnipeg: OPP
stories.summary: A 28-year-old man wanted in connection with a murder in Bolton five years ago has been arrested, hours after he was named one of Canada’s 25 Most Wanted fugitives. Ontario Provincial Police say Filmon Fesshaghirgis of London, Ont., was arrested in Winnipeg on Thursday by members of the RCMP and Winnipeg Police Service.

stories.headline: Inside the historic summit between Trump, Xi and Putin
stories.summary: It was the summit seen around the world. The first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia resulted in a joint statement that included promises to release more oil and hold formal talks about nuclear weapons.
